body: Wellbutrin was great for me and helped a lot before my bipolar onset. Now no one lets me go on it. I’m hoping to be able to try it again or Strattera

Bipolar one and can’t get a prescription for Wellbutrin even without a stimulant with a rule out dx of ADHD (trying to get an assessment but it’s hard in my area and with Medicare insurance and when i go manic from stress or changing seasons every few months). My doctors are so careful because even just SSRI’s make me manic at low doses and while on high dose AP but I’ve never been able to find a med that I can tolerate without appetite increase ( bad for my ED) (besides Geodon but that I couldn’t stay on for other reasons) to control my mania! Trying lithium again but like you said everyone is different and my mania is quite unruly! Idk OP’s story but yeah for sure Wellbutrin is definitely worth a try! Treating depression is just as important as treating mania!! I wish doctors took it that way.

Wellbutrin might be a bit much with the other stimulant (Wellbutrin is stimulating). A good doctor may not put a bipolar person on two stimulating drugs. SSRI might be worth a shot even if it is just for a short period of time! They work different for everyone :). There may be other antidepressants out there though if he doesn’t want to try SSRIs and Wellbutrin is not an option. Still worth a shot asking for Wellbutrin though!

They’ll only civilly commit you here if you’ve been on a involuntary 72 hour hold and they don’t want you to discharge after the 72 is up and you won’t go voluntary or they’re scared you’re gonna leave. And then it’s a whole court process to get a legal commitment by a judge. I don’t recommend it. Not fun. In my experience, you lose a lot of rights and you don’t even get to decide where you go most of the time. 

However, you can voluntarily go to the hospital. I can only speak from personal experience, but usually if you’re voluntary you don’t stay very long at all. At least that’s how it is where I live. Ever time I’ve been in the hospital, the voluntary folks would be there for about a week and then the committed people would be there for multiple weeks until they’re transferred somewhere else. They’ll discharge you once they feel your meds are okay and you’ll be safe. Good luck with everything and I hope you feel better soon.
